emotional: Mina carried her washing into the basement after lunch. The fluorescent tube hummed above three machines, and rain ticked against the pavement window. She sorted socks without looking at their colors. Even the red pair seemed to belong to somebody with a more interesting life. When a washer finished, she watched its drum stop before remembering to open it. There was nothing wrong with the afternoon that she could explain. That made its weight harder to shift. She folded the towels slowly and climbed upstairs, already certain that the rooms above would offer more of the same.
neutral: Mina carried her washing into the basement after lunch. The fluorescent tube lit three machines, and rain reached the pavement window. emotional: The kettle clicked off while Arun stood beside the office sink. He poured water into a mug and watched the tea spread through it. neutral: Before opening the seed shop, Tenzin arranged packets along the counter. The illustrations showed vegetables in several colors against the brown shelves. neutral: At closing time, Esther wheeled returned books toward their shelves. A travel guide fell open to a mountain path, and she flattened its page with her palm. neutral: Bao removed a bowl from the pottery studio's collection shelf. The glaze had settled into blue rings around its base, as the instructor had predicted. neutral: Along the canal, Otto stopped to tighten the lace of his walking shoe. The water carried a paper cup beneath a footbridge and past a row of moored boats.
